findings.reason: the design must specify an order-preserving return (an ordered sequence of `(identity, prose)` slices, not a bare mapping) or the whole-document form's byte-parity requirement is unsatisfiable on the three plans measured.
findings.text: the design returns prose "keyed by identity with the remainder under the document unit", but `_fingerprint_forms` must join "the slices' prose in document order, sections and the remainder alike" and `authored_plan_text` "joins them in document order"; measured on this project, 3 of 151 plans carry non-empty authored remainder interleaved between sections (clive-local-workers.html — 5 remainder slices, project-state-fleet-migration.html — 4, sprint-horizon-surface.html — 3), so a single `_document` bucket loses their position and the claimed byte-identity with the deleted parser cannot hold on those plans

findings.reason: an implementer scoping node 2 from this prose would search `plan_review.py` for the skip set and look for a keyword to add, finding neither pending, so the plan must correct its account of what node 1 already delivered before the node is released.
findings.text: the plan's own account of what remains is wrong: it says "the skip set, `_PROSE_SKIP_TAGS`, is owned today by `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` and moves with the job into `reckon/_plan_html.py`, private as before", but `_PROSE_SKIP_TAGS` is already defined at `reckon/_plan_html.py:1877` and no such name exists in `reckon/crew/plan_review.py`; it likewise says `structured_section_spans` "gains the keyword `every_marked_element`", but `reckon/_plan_html.py:418` already carries that keyword (and `skip_landed_cards`)

findings.reason: add a check that `_prose_slices` no longer exists, or the consolidation ships a second slicer the gate cannot see, which is the drift the design exists to prevent.
findings.text: `_prose_slices` is the slicer the design replaces with `section_prose`, and its two consumers (`_section_digests`, `_fingerprint_forms`) are repointed, but no done-when requires `_prose_slices` to be removed; it can survive as a one-line delegator to `section_prose` while every named grep (`def section_prose`, `read_plan_review(`, `stripped_strings`, `_TAG_RE`, `_PROSE_SKIP_TAGS`) still passes

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the proposed `section_prose` interface, "keyed by identity with the remainder under the document unit", cannot carry the document-order whole-document prose the design requires of it, because the remainder does not form one contiguous bucket.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the design consolidates the duplicate prose readers (`mcp_views.authored_plan_text`, `mcp_views._section_response`, the `plan_review` slicer) into one owner, `section_prose` on `reckon/_plan_html.py`, and reads `roadmap.implementable_sections` (`reckon/roadmap.py:107`) and `list_plan_reviews` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:618`) unchanged rather than re-implementing them.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 names the one public definition it retires (`strip_tags` made private as `_strip_tags`) against the one it adds (`section_prose`), for a net of zero, and §20 adds none, so each adding section accounts for its surface in its own text.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan does cite the machinery it extends, but its account of the prior art for its remaining node is stale: §16 says `_PROSE_SKIP_TAGS` is owned today by `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` and "moves ... into `reckon/_plan_html.py`", and that `structured_section_spans` "gains the keyword `every_marked_element`", yet both already hold on `reckon/_plan_html.py` (node 1 landed them).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the design repoints `_prose_slices`'s consumers to `section_prose` but names no check that `_prose_slices` is deleted rather than left as a delegator, so a redundant second slicer would pass every named done-when.
